text: Ear discharge: A presenting complaint characterised by ear discharge.
Ear pain: Ear pain, also known as earache or otalgia, is pain in the ear. Primary ear pain is pain that originates from the ear.

Mouth ulcers: A mouth ulcer (aphtha), or sometimes called a canker sore or salt blister, is an ulcer that occurs on the mucous membrane of the oral cavity. Mouth ulcers are very common, occurring in association with many diseases and by many different mechanisms, but usually there is no serious underlying cause.

Nasal congestion: Nasal congestion is the partial or complete blockage of nasal passages, leading to impaired nasal breathing, usually due to membranes lining the nose becoming swollen from inflammation of blood vessels, or an excess of mucus in the sinuses caused by illnesses like the common cold.

Rhinorrhoea: Rhinorrhea, also spelled rhinorrhoea or rhinorrhœa, or informally, runny nose, is the free discharge of a thin mucus fluid from the nose; it is an extremely common condition. It is a common symptom of allergies or certain viral infections, such as the common cold or COVID-19.
Sore throat: Sore throat, also known as throat pain, is pain or irritation of the throat. The majority of sore throats are caused by a virus, for which antibiotics are not helpful.

Tinnitus: Tinnitus is a condition when a person hears a ringing sound or a different variety of sounds when no corresponding external sound is present and that other people cannot hear. The word tinnitus comes from the Latin tinnire, "to ring".

Acute otitis media: Otitis media is a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear. One of the two main types is acute otitis media (AOM), an infection of rapid onset that usually presents with ear pain. Common presenting complaints: Ear Pain, Ear Discharge. Associated symptoms: Ear Pain, Fever, Hearing Loss, Ear Fullness. Risk factors: Young Children, Daycare Attendance, Bottle Feeding. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
Acute otitis media red flags. Red flag (RF_ACUTE_MASTOIDITIS) triggered by symptom 'POSTAURICULAR_SWELLING': Swelling and redness behind the ear.

Acute pharyngitis: Pharyngitis is inflammation of the back of the throat, known as the pharynx. It typically results in a sore throat and fever. Common presenting complaints: Sore Throat. Associated symptoms: Sore Throat, Fever, Pharyngeal Erythema, Dysphagia. Risk factors: Viral Exposure, Close Contact. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
Acute pharyngitis red flags. Red flag (RF_SEVERE_DEHYDRATION) triggered by symptom 'DECREASED_URINE': Inability to swallow liquids resulting in dehydration.

Acute sinusitis: Sinusitis, also known as rhinosinusitis and commonly known as a sinus infection, is an inflammation of the mucous membranes that line the sinuses resulting in symptoms that may include production of thick nasal mucus, nasal congestion, facial congestion, facial pain, facial pressure, loss of smell, or fever. Common presenting complaints: Nasal Congestion. Associated symptoms: Nasal Congestion, Facial Pain Pressure, Purulent Nasal Discharge, Headache. Risk factors: Preceding Viral Uri, Nasal Polyps. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
Acute sinusitis red flags. Red flag (RF_ORBITAL_CELLULITIS) triggered by symptom 'PERIORBITAL_EDEMA': Swelling or redness around the eye.

Acute tonsillitis: Tonsillitis is inflammation of the tonsils in the upper part of the throat. It can be acute or chronic. Common presenting complaints: Sore Throat. Associated symptoms: Severe Sore Throat, Tonsillar Exudate, High Fever, Cervical Lymphadenopathy. Risk factors: Streptococcal Infection, Young Age. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
Acute tonsillitis red flags. Red flag (RF_PERITONSILLAR_ABSCESS) triggered by symptom 'TRISMUS': Inability to open mouth fully or muffled voice.

Allergic rhinitis: Allergic rhinitis, of which the seasonal type is called hay fever, is a type of inflammation in the nose that occurs when the immune system overreacts to allergens in the air. It is classified as a type I hypersensitivity reaction. Common presenting complaints: Nasal Congestion, Rhinorrhoea. Associated symptoms: Nasal Congestion, Rhinorrhoea, Sneezing, Nasal Itching. Risk factors: Atopy, Family History Allergy, Pollen Exposure. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Aphthous stomatitis: Aphthous stomatitis, or recurrent aphthous stomatitis (RAS), commonly referred to as a canker sore or salt blister, is a common condition characterized by the repeated formation of benign and non-contagious mouth ulcers (aphthae) in otherwise healthy individuals. Common presenting complaints: Mouth Ulcers. Associated symptoms: Oral Ulcers, Mouth Pain, Dysphagia. Risk factors: Stress, Nutritional Deficiency, Trauma To Oral Mucosa. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Chronic suppurative otitis media: Otitis media is a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear. One of the two main types is acute otitis media (AOM), an infection of rapid onset that usually presents with ear pain. Common presenting complaints: Ear Discharge. Associated symptoms: Otorrhoea, Hearing Loss, Tinnitus. Risk factors: Recurrent Otitis Media, Eustachian Tube Dysfunction. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Otitis externa: Otitis externa, also called swimmer's ear, is inflammation of the ear canal. It often presents with ear pain, swelling of the ear canal, and occasionally decreased hearing. Common presenting complaints: Ear Pain. Associated symptoms: Ear Canal Pain, Ear Discharge, Ear Itching, Tragus Tenderness. Risk factors: Swimming, Ear Canal Trauma, Diabetes. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
Otitis externa red flags. Red flag (RF_NECROTIZING_OTITIS) triggered by symptom 'SEVERE_EAR_PAIN': Severe, deep ear pain especially in diabetics or immunocompromised.

This commonly includes nasal obstruction, sore throat, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, laryngitis, sinusitis, otitis media, and the common cold. Common presenting complaints: Rhinorrhoea, Nasal Congestion.
